title: RunConfiguration
description: Top-level configuration file that controls a full dataset generation run. Composes the Step 2 (environment), Step 3 (categories), Step 4 (patterns), Step 5 (selection rules), and Step 6 (protocol/codec) artifacts via a base-scenario + override pattern, and adds dataset_size, which none of those steps owned individually.

record_count.description: Required for single_environment or per_environment modes.

environment_weights.description: Optional, total_target mode only. Maps environment_id -> proportion of total_records. Defaults to an equal split across environments if omitted.

observation_period_overrides.description: Step 2 §i shape. Optional if base_scenario is a named profile; required (in full) if base_scenario=custom.

roles.description: Step 2 organizational_structure.roles shape. Optional for custom scenarios - if omitted, one department-agnostic (department: '*') role is synthesized per role_distribution key, giving a flat weighted draw with no per-department eligibility. Provide this explicitly for department-specific role eligibility (e.g. an admin-only role restricted to one department). When provided, role ids should be Step 1's canonical user_role vocabulary directly (student/faculty/administrative_staff/manager/employee/customer_support_agent/customer/dispatcher/external_contact), since custom scenarios have no separate org-role-to-canonical-role mapping step.

department.description: A department id, or '*' for department-agnostic (eligible everywhere).

network_configuration_overrides.description: Step 2 §vi shape. Optional for named profiles (inherited from the base scenario). Optional for custom scenarios too, with a graceful fallback: if omitted, a single synthesized internal CIDR (10.99.0.0/16) with no per-department segmentation is used (see run_config_resolver.py's module docstring). Provide this explicitly for a custom scenario that needs real per-department network segmentation.

user_attribute_overrides.description: Step 1 population_by_environment shape (config/users/user_population_characteristics.json) — gap fix: Step 9 originally had no way to override Step 1's per-user attribute distributions at all, since Step 9 predates Step 1 existing as a formal deliverable in this project. Overrides here replace entries in Step 1's population characteristics for this environment.

role_distribution.description: Keys from Step 1's canonical user_role vocabulary. If provided, must sum to 1.0.

active_hours_distribution.description: Keys are shift-preset labels (e.g. 'standard_business', 'night_shift'); values are selection weights.

default_external_role.description: Which canonical role external users default to. Gap fix: this was previously hardcoded in code as a check against the literal environment name 'emergency_response', which silently broke for any renamed environment_id or custom scenario.

communication_category_overrides.description: Step 3 §3 shape — full or partial replacement of the environment's category_mix. Keys are category ids from communication_categories.json; if provided, must sum to 1.0.

communication_pattern_overrides.description: Step 4 shape — keyed by category_id, partial override of that category's pattern profile (e.g. duration band, temporal shape). Rare in practice; patterns are largely category-intrinsic rather than environment-specific.

protocol_distribution_overrides.description: Step 6 §5.3 shape — replaces the environment's signaling/media protocol weights.

codec_distribution_overrides.description: Step 6 §5.3 shape — replaces the environment's codec weight table. If provided, must sum to 1.0 across included codecs.

relationship_rule_overrides.description: Step 5 §5 shape — replaces mechanism_weights and/or relationship_type_mix for this environment.

validation_notes.environment_id_uniqueness: Every environment_id in environments[] must be unique within the run configuration.
validation_notes.distribution_sums: communication_category_overrides, codec_distribution_overrides, and relationship_type_mix, when provided, must each sum to 1.0 +/- 0.001. protocol_distribution_overrides' SIP+H.323 pair and RTP+SRTP pair must each sum to 1.0 +/- 0.001 independently.
validation_notes.dataset_size_mode_consistency: single_environment and per_environment modes require record_count; total_target mode requires total_records.
validation_notes.single_environment_mode: dataset_size.mode=single_environment is only valid when environments[] has exactly one entry.
